name: Contradictory Thinker
description: A person holding genuinely conflicting beliefs — the kind of cognitive dissonance most people carry without realizing it. The map should be dominated by red (tension and contradiction).
beliefs: Free will is the basis of moral responsibility
Every event is determined by prior causes — nothing is truly random
Objective moral truths exist independently of human opinion
Morality is entirely a social construct that varies by culture
Science gives us objective knowledge of reality
All knowledge is ultimately subjective and perspectival
Humans are fundamentally selfish by nature
People are naturally cooperative and altruistic
Consciousness is nothing more than brain activity
There is a soul or spirit that transcends the physical body

justifications.0-1: Free will as the basis of moral responsibility is contradicted by hard determinism — if every event has prior causes, libertarian free will cannot exist.
justifications.2-3: Objective moral truths independent of human opinion cannot coexist with the claim that morality is entirely a social construct varying by culture.
justifications.4-5: The belief that science gives objective knowledge directly contradicts radical subjectivism about all knowledge.
justifications.6-7: Fundamental human selfishness is logically incompatible with the claim that humans are naturally cooperative and altruistic.
justifications.8-9: Reductive physicalism about consciousness (it's just brain activity) contradicts belief in a non-physical soul or spirit.
justifications.0-8: Free will is difficult to reconcile with the view that consciousness is merely brain activity, since brain processes are typically seen as deterministic.
justifications.1-8: Determinism and physicalist consciousness are mutually reinforcing — both describe a world governed entirely by physical causation.
justifications.2-4: Objective moral truths and scientific objectivism both posit mind-independent facts that can be discovered.
